name: n52b30_3l_na
source: BMW N52B30 3.0 L naturally aspirated DOHC 24V gasoline I6 (2,996 cc, 85 mm bore x 88 mm stroke, compression ratio 10.7:1, redline 7000 rpm) - the 190 kW (255 bhp) at 6600 rpm / 300 N*m at 2500-4000 rpm variant fitted to the 2009-2015 F01 730i, 2008-2011 E89 Z4 sDrive30i, 2009-2011 E84 X1 xDrive28i, 2009-2012 E87 130i, 2010-2011 F25 X3 28i and 2010-2011 F10 528i/530i (Asia/Europe) - per Wikipedia's BMW N52 article's own spec table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_N52, fetched 2026-09-27), citation-per-point below. Two points are PUBLISHED: the 300 N*m plateau across 2500-4000 rpm (x=2500/3000/3500/4000, y=300, the table's torque figure for this variant, flat across its stated rpm band) and the single power point 190 kW at 6600 rpm, converted to a torque figure via T = P*60/(2*pi*n) = 190000*60/(2*pi*6600) = 274.9 N*m, rounded to 275 (x=6600, y=275) - not itself a published torque number, but a direct unit conversion of one. EVERY OTHER POINT IS ASSUMED (hand-shaped to blend smoothly between those two anchors in a typical NA-I6 rising-then-falling shape, the same way i4_2l_na.json's own curve was hand-shaped around its own two anchor regions - not read off a manufacturer dyno chart, no such chart cited by the source above): the low-rpm rise 500-2000 rpm (140/220/260/285, roughly the i4_2l_na.json template's own 500-2000 rpm values scaled by this engine's ~1.5x displacement ratio, 3.0/2.0 L); the gentle post-peak decline 4500-6500 rpm (296/292/288/282/277) bridging the 300 N*m plateau down to the derived 275 N*m point at 6600; and the 7000 rpm value (230), assumed fall-off approaching the 7000 rpm redline (breathing/valve-float losses, not measured). inertia_kgm2 0.25: ASSUMED, i4_2l_na.json's 0.16 kg*m^2 (crank+flywheel+clutch cover, 2.0 L I4) scaled ~1.56x for a longer 6-cylinder crank - no published N52 rotating-inertia figure found. breakaway_torque_nm 65.0: ASSUMED, i4_2l_na.json's 45.0 scaled by the same displacement ratio (>= -motoring_torque_nm_vs_rpm(0) = 22, satisfied). motoring_torque_nm_vs_rpm: ASSUMED, i4_2l_na.json's own Heywood-correlation-derived curve scaled by 1.5x displacement ratio and rounded (not an independent Heywood fmep derivation for this specific bore/stroke - see that file's own source field for the underlying correlation and citation). idle_rpm 750 (ASSUMED, typical modern BMW I6 curb-idle target, no source-cited figure for this exact variant), stall_rpm 400/fire_rpm 220/start_complete_rpm 550/dfco thresholds 1300/1000: ASSUMED, i4_2l_na.json's own template values (unmodified; satisfies the stall<start_complete<=idle<limiter ordering rule). idle_control gains: ASSUMED, unmodified from i4_2l_na.json's own tuning (not retuned for this engine's inertia - owner ruling for this pass is 'don't overthink', only the clutch is tested; retune by ear if idle hunts). limiter fuel_cut at 6900 rpm (ASSUMED, just under the cited 7000 rpm redline), hysteresis_rpm 150 (ASSUMED, i4_2l_na.json's template value). starter stall_torque_nm 160.0 (ASSUMED, i4_2l_na.json's 140.0 scaled up slightly for a larger engine), free_speed_rpm 400.0/interlock clutch_or_neutral (ASSUMED, unmodified template values). crank_axis_local [0,1,0]: same chassis-local Y (ISO left) mounting axis as i4_2l_na.json - the chassis/gearbox orientation is unchanged, only the engine swapped.
